doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

chapter: Playboy Club and the working life
title: Hearing chords, guitar harmony and relative pitch
summary: Gafa disputes that guitarists play chords without knowing them, explaining how he hears and adjusts voicings; he has good relative pitch.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I had an incident once and it always sticks in my mind, playing in a rock band, but the guitar player was just — played the most beautiful chords and he played something one night and I asked him what it was, what chord is that, because I play piano also. And he held up his hand, he said, “It’s this.” And I said, “Well that doesn’t really help me, can you tell me what the notes are?” And he really couldn’t. He would have to like laboriously look at each string and figure oh okay. But I don’t really have a question here except that guitar seems to be an instrument that you can play a lot of hip chords and so forth and maybe not know exactly what they are? Is that a fair statement?

Not to me, no. It’s not really fair. Because if a piano player plays a chord I can hear all the notes in the chord. And there are certain notes when you play a chord, they’re volatile, they want to move in one direction or another, so you’re kind of ready, you can anticipate where they’re going to go. If you’re wrong, you have to make a minor adjustment to fix it. And it’s not a big deal. Or on a guitar from playing a three note chord and I hear that one of these notes is not the same thing I just stop that note from ringing and it’s over. And the time is — it’s such a short amount of time most people wouldn’t even hear — you know I could stop it in the middle of striking with my right hand so I know what to do in those situations. My ear is pretty good so I hear when a piano player plays something I immediately know.
Would you say you have relative pitch?
Yeah. Relative is good. Yeah. It’s not perfect.
